author: sme-bastion (independent technology SME critic, Claude Opus 5.5 subagent)

findings.claim: The teaching gives 'a local variable of a method that has not returned' as the example of what keeps an object reachable. The JLS explicitly allows a compiler or code generator to treat a variable that will no longer be used as dead, so an object referenced only by such a local can become unreachable before the method returns. A learner taking the example literally would assume an in-scope local guarantees an object stays alive (for example to keep a resource or listener alive), which practitioners meet as early collection. The surrounding phrase 'a variable that running code can still use' is correct; only the example overstates. Activity 3's key (Box 1 and Box 4) is right under the naive model the page teaches.
findings.recommendation: Change the example to 'such as a local variable that the method may still read', or add one sentence: 'The JVM may treat a variable the code will never read again as gone, so do not rely on a local to keep an object alive.'
